name: Moghul Ganjifa
description: Moghul Ganjifa is a traditional South Asian trick-taking game family played with the 96-card Mughal ganjifa deck and circular-suited court structure.

overview.description: Moghul Ganjifa is a traditional South Asian trick-taking game family played with the 96-card Mughal ganjifa deck and circular-suited court structure.

history.origins: Doppen appears in Austrian tarock references as a real regional tarock game in the broader Industrie und Glück branch.
timeline: Historical period: Austrian tarock variants spread in central Europe.
Modern references: Doppen listed in tarot game indexes and regional rules collections.
history.cultural: Doppen belongs to coffeehouse and club tarock culture where table rules are precise and trick counting is emphasized.
history.evolution: It shares core tarock mechanics with related Austrian games while using local contract and talon conventions.

setup.players: Typically 2-6 players depending on local ganjifa variant.
setup.deck: 54-card Industrie und Glück pack with 22 permanent trumps and 32 suited cards.
setup.dealing: Cards are dealt with a talon packet according to local Doppen dealing conventions before contract decisions.

rules.objective: Win enough card points under the chosen contract by taking tricks and controlling key trumps.
rules.gameplay: Players follow suit when possible, otherwise play trump when required, and otherwise discard. Highest trump wins trumped tricks; otherwise highest card in the led suit wins. Contract and talon handling determine risk and reward each deal.
keyRules: Three-player tarock with contracts and tarot trump hierarchy.
Suit-follow obligations apply before discretionary discard.
Talon decisions influence declarer strength and defender counterplay.

strategy.basic: Preserve high trumps and avoid conceding point-rich tricks early.
strategy.intermediate: Use talon information to rebalance suit length and create controlled trump entries.
strategy.advanced: Optimize contract selection against hand texture and expected defender pressure while counting trumps and honors.
tips: Do not overcommit trumps before point-critical tricks.
Track exposed honors to estimate remaining trick equity.

variations.name: Local contract scale
variations.description: Some groups use slightly different contract ladders and values.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes local scoring profile, not the base engine structure.

scoring.description: Scoring follows Austrian tarock contract outcomes and card-point counting.
scoring.winCondition: Highest valid score under the agreed contract and counting rules wins the deal or session.

synthesis.shortDescription: Doppen is a three-player Austrian tarock game in the Industrie und Glück family with contract and talon pressure.
